subtopics.title: Momentum and Newton's Second Law in Momentum Form

questions.question: Linear momentum is defined as:
options: The product of an object's mass and its velocity
The product of an object's mass and its acceleration
The force needed to stop an object
The energy an object has because of its motion

questions.question: A 1 200 kg bakkie travels at 20 m·s⁻¹ east. Its momentum is:
A 0,5 kg ball hits a wall at 10 m·s⁻¹ and rebounds at 8 m·s⁻¹. Taking toward the wall as positive, its change in momentum is:
Newton's second law in terms of momentum states that the net force equals:
options: The change in momentum multiplied by the time taken
The total momentum of the system
The rate of change of momentum

questions.question: The impulse-momentum theorem states that FnetΔt equals:
options: mΔv, the change in momentum of the object
½mv², the kinetic energy of the object
ma, the net force on the object
mgh, the potential energy of the object

questions.question: A 0,16 kg cricket ball arrives at 30 m·s⁻¹ and is driven straight back at 40 m·s⁻¹. The magnitude of the impulse on the ball is:
If that impulse of 11,2 N·s is delivered in 0,01 s, the average net force on the ball is:
An airbag reduces injury in a crash because it:
options: Reduces the change in momentum of the head
Increases the momentum of the car
Increases the time over which the momentum changes, reducing the net force

questions.question: The principle of conservation of linear momentum applies to a system that is:
options: Isolated — no net external force acts on it

questions.question: During a collision, the forces the two objects exert on each other cannot change the total momentum because they are:
options: Too brief to have an effect
Equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, acting inside the system

questions.question: A 4 kg rifle at rest fires a 0,02 kg bullet at 400 m·s⁻¹. The rifle's recoil velocity is:
After the rifle fires, the bullet and rifle have:

subtopics.title: Collisions in One Dimension — Elastic or Inelastic

questions.question: A 2 kg trolley at 3 m·s⁻¹ hits a stationary 1 kg trolley and they couple. Their common velocity is:
An elastic collision is one in which:
options: The objects bounce apart without touching

questions.question: In the trolley collision, kinetic energy drops from 9 J to 6 J. The correct conclusion is:
options: The calculation must be wrong, since energy cannot disappear
The collision was inelastic — 3 J became heat, sound and deformation

questions.question: Which quantity is conserved in BOTH elastic and inelastic collisions in an isolated system?

subtopics.title: Moving Oomph — Why Mass and Speed Both Count

questions.question: A cricket ball is harder to catch than a tennis ball at the same speed because it has:
options: More momentum, because it has more mass

questions.question: A slow, fully loaded coal truck can carry more momentum than a fast pellet because:
options: Momentum is mass times velocity, and its huge mass outweighs its low speed

questions.question: A ball bouncing off a wall changes its momentum MORE than one that stops dead because:
options: It must lose all its forward momentum AND gain momentum in the opposite direction
The wall pushes only on bouncing balls

questions.question: An egg thrown at a duvet survives while one thrown at a wall breaks. The duvet:
options: Reduces the egg's change in momentum
Stretches the stopping time, so the force on the egg is smaller

questions.question: In every impulse safety question, the quantity that stays FIXED during the stop is:
Which of the following works on a DIFFERENT principle from the other three?
options: A seatbelt preventing a passenger from continuing forward
A crumple zone folding in a crash
A fielder pulling the hands back during a catch
A gravel arrestor bed stopping a runaway truck

questions.question: The full-marks explanation for any impulse safety device has three steps, in this order:
options: Force is smaller; time is longer; momentum change is fixed
The device is soft; the crash is slower; the person is safer
Momentum change is fixed; the time is increased; therefore the force is smaller
Energy is absorbed; momentum is destroyed; force disappears

questions.question: A loaded trolley with 6 units of momentum locks onto a stationary trolley. Just after the crash, the pair's total momentum is:
options: 6 units, shared over the combined mass
3 units, because it is shared between two trolleys
12 units, because there are now two trolleys

questions.question: Momentum is conserved during the crash because the trolleys:
options: Move too fast for friction to act
Only exert equal and opposite forces on each other, inside the system

questions.question: Trolleys that stick together after a collision always give:
options: An inelastic collision — some kinetic energy is lost
A collision where momentum is not conserved

questions.question: The only way to decide whether a collision is elastic is to:
options: Calculate total kinetic energy before and after and compare
